summary: Tests-only red-phase PR for issue #39 delivered: committed the color_matching parity corpus (v1, 12 scenarios: 5 tie-break, 4 exclusion, 2 no-selection, 1 zero-error) as a test fixture and wrote SolverParityCorpusTests (exact replay through WeightedSquaredErrorScorer), PaletteAPIWireContractTests (wire pins the generated-client migration must preserve), OpenAPIClientAdoptionTests (red: swift-openapi-generator/runtime deps + committed OpenAPI document), and OfflineFallbackAfterFetchTests (fetch -> disk cache -> offline identity, per-server namespacing, picker fallback), plus docs/parity-corpus.md. swift test could NOT be executed: no Swift toolchain exists in this container (no swift/xcrun; not installable). Parity replay semantics were validated 1:1 against the committed fixture with an equivalent Python simulation of the scorer (exact scores, 'excluded' mapping, earliest-index-wins selection, tied_indices, tie_broke): 0 mismatches across all 12 scenarios. /api/v1 shape findings for the PR description: both consumed endpoints are unchanged upstream (GET /api/v1/printer_profiles, GET /api/v1/colors?printer_profile_id=N, envelopes {printer_profiles:[...]} and {printer_profile, colors:[...]}); the published OpenAPI spec (GET /api/v1/openapi.json) marks printer_make_model/paper_type/ink_type required and printer_profile present in ColorsResponse, where current Swift DTOs treat them optional - the wrapper must keep tolerating absence to preserve disk-cache compatibility. Implementation criteria land in the follow-up run after paid-tests-approved.
